title: An Agent-Based Model of Rural Households' Adaptation to Climate Change
publisher: Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation (JASSS) 21(4) 4; Hailegiorgis, Crooks, Cioffi-Revilla

key_points.claim: OMOLAND-CA is an ABM of rural household adaptation to climate change in South Omo Zone, Ethiopia. It explicitly represents agents' socio-cognitive behavior and resource flows.
key_points.evidence_quote: Our model explicitly represents the socio-cognitive behavior of rural households toward climate change and resource flows that prompt agents to diversify their production strategy

key_points.claim: Agent cognition and decision-making are built on the MPPACC framework, which the authors say has been largely neglected in adaptation research.
key_points.evidence_quote: the role of cognition in adaptation to climate change has so far been largely neglected

key_points.claim: Implementation and reproducibility: the model was built in MASON with GeoMASON (GIS), with code, data and an ODD+D description published on CoMSES.
key_points.evidence_quote: The model was implemented in the MASON simulation system, including its geographical information system (GIS) extension, GeoMASON

key_points.claim: Environment and population: the model uses spatial datasets and covers roughly 570,000 people in 125,000 households. Births and deaths are modeled at household level and affect labor allocation.

Results on resilience and migration: successive extreme events erode assets and adaptive capacity and push households to migrate. Mixed herding-farming strategies survive best. Accurate drought prediction matters a great deal but is hard to achieve.
key_points.evidence_quote: mixed strategies provide a superior survival advantage for households facing the harsh challenges of climate change

key_points.claim: Validation is a limitation. The model passes face-validity tests only. Data scarcity, especially in developing countries, hampers empirical validation.
key_points.evidence_quote: more rigorous empirical validation is necessary to ensure the robustness of the emerging patterns

key_points.claim: Future work: agent behavior around technology adoption, trust in climate forecasts, and family cohesion or cooperation.
key_points.evidence_quote: explore the willingness of rural households to adopt new agricultural technology and climate adaptation measures

key_points.claim: The authors argue that ABM suits representing human decision-making and human-environment interaction, and that ABMs work as computational laboratories.
key_points.evidence_quote: Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) is a natural way of representing socio-cognitive behavior of individuals and simulating complex interactions between individuals and their environment

reliability_notes: Full text of a peer-reviewed, open-access JASSS article. It is a domain-specific case study (climate adaptation) rather than a general review of artificial societies. Quotes come from the introduction, background, and discussion sections. I did not read the results section in detail.
